title: Methods
goal: In this lesson you will learn how methods are functions inside a class that you call with a dot.
learn: Write a method with def inside the class
Methods can print or change data
idea: A method is a function that lives inside a class. You call it with a dot: dog.bark(). For now, include self as the first parameter (next lesson explains why). Methods let objects do things, not only store data.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the name to "Luna". Press Run. Output should say Luna says woof!

practice.text: Finish greet so it prints a hello using self.name. Call it once.
practice.hint: Inside greet, use print with self.name — the Player's name is set on p before you call p.greet().
practice.starterTip: In the blank under greet, try: print("Hello,", self.name) — then run; Ava's name should appear.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if greet uses self.name and prints a hello for Ava.

practice.text: Add a method spin that prints Weee! Call it on a Toy object.
practice.hint: The spin method body needs one indented print line. t.spin() at the bottom calls it.
practice.starterTip: Inside spin, add: print("Weee!") — indented under def spin(self):.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if spin method prints Weee! when called.

quiz.question: How do you call bark on dog?
First parameter of a method is usually…
quiz.correct: self means this object — next lesson!
